unresolved.finding: The image tags, yum packages, pip mmi dependency, and xbeach-mi branch are all unpinned, so identical source builds can resolve to different binary and Python dependency sets.
The runtime fixes Python at 3.4 while installing unrestricted mmi and a moving xbeach-mi branch, without constraining either package to versions supporting that interpreter.
The shell-form CMD launches mmi-runner without exec, leaving a shell as PID 1 that may not forward container termination signals to the simulation.
The list placeholder inserts markup directly into the page without specifying that its producer must escape any filename-derived link text and attribute values.
The page has neither a document type declaration nor a title, leaving browser rendering mode and the page's tab or assistive-technology label unspecified.
The scalar-allocation description requires instantiation before array allocation but does not state that dimension scalars also need defined values before they are used as bounds.

The final ./makeincludes example does not provide the end-of-file that the earlier empty-standard-input example supplies, so an interactive invocation may wait for input instead of generating all files.
The command git commit -a . combines automatic all-tracked-file selection with a pathspec, which Git rejects.
The push commands use . and somepage.rst as repository arguments, so they do not publish the commits to the cloned remote.
The SVN checkout command reuses the Git clone endpoint ending in .git without identifying an SVN-compatible endpoint or bridge.
The displayed installation sequence runs make distclean after configure and then immediately runs make without regenerating the configuration and Makefiles.
The master-only readkey example does not explain how its result reaches other ranks when the parameter is needed outside the master.
The documented saved scratch-array pattern allocates only once and explicitly leaves wrong-sized arrays possible when subsequent spacepar instances have different dimensions.
The recommendation to omit zero initialization provides no requirement that every array element be assigned before use, although allocation alone does not initialize real values.
The suggested trial substitution of MPI libraries changes the documented calling convention without requiring matching compiler ABI settings.
The example identifies 1.2d0 as the intended nontruncated result of 5/4, but the correct value is 1.25d0.

The text attributes power-of-two multiplication and division optimizations to integer literal spelling even though the equivalent double-precision constants are exactly representable and can support the same optimizations.
The nf90_create synopsis omits initialsize and chunksize although both appear in its argument declarations, leaving their positional order unspecified.
References to nf__open, nf__enddef, and nf90_varinq do not match the corresponding Fortran-90 routines documented in this manual.
The nf90_def_var declarations omit the varid output and show only an array dimids declaration despite explicitly supporting a scalar dimids argument.
The nf90_inquire_variable explanation treats scalar ndims as an array containing dimension IDs and applies SIZE to it, conflating ndims with dimids.
The nf90_rename_var declaration contains invalid intent9in) syntax and declares newname where the synopsis uses name.

The variable read/write signatures jump directly from start to stride and provide no count argument or explanation of how transfer extents are selected, making positional use and partial-array transfers ambiguous.
The attribute inquiry describes xtype as the variable's external type although the queried object is an attribute whose type can differ.
The get_att synopsis splits its font escape incorrectly, and the rename_att section leaves its RS indentation unclosed before the next routine.

The common dimids description permits a vector larger than the variable rank without distinguishing inquiry output capacity from definition input, whereas nf90_def_var says every supplied element contributes a dimension.

The manual recommends OR-ing nf90_nofill into open/create mode despite omitting it from both routines' flag lists, leaving that alternative to nf90_set_fill unsupported by the documented creation/opening contracts.
The filter discards every line containing warning: followed later by mpi_, potentially hiding substantive MPI warnings without limiting suppression to a known benign diagnostic.
The unconditional successful exit also masks grep execution or input/output errors, beyond neutralizing grep's ordinary no-selected-lines status.
The newline-delimited find output is passed to whitespace-splitting xargs, so filenames containing spaces, quotes, or newlines can be split or rejected during removal.
The config/* removal also targets the shard's config/index_bin.html.tmpl source template although the script claims to remove autoconf-generated files.
All removal targets are relative to the caller's current directory without a repository-root check, so invoking the script from another directory can delete unrelated matching files.
An empty compatibility element is nested inside dependentAssembly despite a separate application compatibility section at lines 10-18, leaving the validity and purpose of the nested element unclear.
SubWCRev values are inserted directly into single-quoted Fortran literals, so a substituted URL containing an apostrophe would break the generated source unless escaping is supplied externally.
